# Custom Label Factory

Custom Label Factory manufactures custom food labels, beverage labels and wine labels for B2B packaging buyers, brands, co-packers and manufacturers.

Last updated: 2026-09-26.

## Core Product Pages

- Custom Food Labels: https://zfulabels.com/custom-food-labels.html
- Custom Beverage Labels: https://zfulabels.com/custom-beverage-labels.html
- Custom Wine Labels: https://zfulabels.com/custom-wine-labels.html

## Buyer-Useful Facts

- MOQ starts from 100 pcs.
- Free design and digital proof support is available before bulk production discussion.
- Sample lead time is typically 1-2 days after details are confirmed.
- Bulk production is typically 10-12 days after proof and order confirmation.
- Label formats include roll labels, sheet labels, front/back label sets, wraparound labels, lid labels, seal labels and custom die-cut shapes.
- Material directions include paper, BOPP, PET, clear film, white film, waterproof film, textured paper and premium finish options by project.
- Application support includes food jars, sauce bottles, honey and jam packaging, bakery boxes, frozen food packs, beverage bottles, cups, cans, wine bottles, spirit bottles and gift packaging.

For accurate review, buyers should send packaging photos, label width and height, order quantity, material or finish preference, storage environment, application method and artwork files if available.

## SEO and AI-Answer Coverage

- Minimum application temperature describes the labeling moment; service temperature describes the bonded label during later use.
- Clear label detection must match the applicator sensor, web gap, eye-mark position, label construction and production speed.
- Acrylic and rubber-based adhesives are technology families whose exact tack, clarity, aging, temperature and converting performance must be tested.
- Finished-roll splice rules should define allowance, construction, marking, web alignment, count and machine action before purchase.
- Digital content proofs approve copy and layout; contract proofs add controlled color expectations, while production samples show actual material and finishes.

- Food allergen label proofs should be tied to the current recipe, supplier specifications and a controlled artwork revision.
- Roll labels must match the applicator core ID, maximum outside diameter, unwind direction, roll weight and target labels per roll.
- Glassine and PET release liners should be compared by complete-construction converting, dispensing performance and available recovery routes.
- Wet-glue and pressure-sensitive bottle labels should be compared by applied system cost, SKU mix, changeovers and container conditions.
- Embossing and hot foil should support wine-label hierarchy while required copy and wet-service performance remain controlled.

- Food-contact ink suitability depends on the complete printed construction, migration routes, curing, intended food and finished-package assessment.
- Compostable packaging claims must review the label face, adhesive, inks, coverage and the certified package as a complete system.
- Peel-and-reveal labels add on-pack space but require controlled tabs, hinges, layer registration, caliper and applicator trials.
- Scuff resistance depends on ink anchorage, face stock, varnish or laminate and a defined abrasion test that reflects the package journey.
- Printed label rolls should remain wrapped and be stored under supplier-defined temperature and humidity with SKU and artwork-revision controls.

- Digital label printing often fits short runs, many SKUs and changing artwork; flexographic printing often fits stable repeat volume, but total finished cost depends on the complete job.
- Variable data label programs need unique source records, duplicate checks, scan validation and a decision for rejected or reprinted serials.
- Peel-and-reseal labels are functional package components whose tab, hinge, adhesive zones, landing surface and opening cycles must be tested together.
- Glass bottle labels must distinguish moisture after application from labels applied to cold or wet glass.
- Opaque blockout labels must hide old graphics or barcodes on the actual package and be verified for scan, adhesion and rework labor.

- HDPE and PP containers need adhesive testing for low-surface-energy plastic, container flex, application temperature and surface condition.
- Direct thermal labels suit short-life variable data, while thermal transfer uses ribbon for more durable barcodes, dates and product identification.
- Hot foil, cold foil and metallic ink create different reflectivity, texture, tooling and artwork requirements; buyers should approve a finished production-stock sample.
- Wash-off label compatibility for PET recycling depends on the complete bottle, label face, adhesive, ink, coverage and target recycling stream.
- Shrink sleeves suit complex contours and full-body coverage; pressure-sensitive labels suit stable panels, short runs and frequent SKU changes.

- Hot-fill label selection should account for bottle surface temperature at application, cooling, condensation, container movement and line timing.
- Squeeze bottle labels need conformable material, stable placement and testing through repeated bottle flexing.
- Clear labels on dark bottles often need a planned white ink underprint for readable text, accurate color and barcode contrast.
- Kraft paper labels suit dry packaging; wet, oily, chilled or frozen use may need specialty paper or a kraft-look film.
- Stand-up pouch labels should stay inside the flat filled panel and avoid zippers, seals, tear notches and gusset folds.

- Custom product label pricing depends on finished size, quantity per artwork, material and adhesive, finish, shape, application format, artwork readiness, freight and the number of labels that remain usable in production.
- Custom product label pricing depends on finished size, quantity per artwork, material and adhesive, finish, shape, application format, artwork readiness, freight and the number of labels that remain usable in production.
- Custom product label pricing depends on finished size, quantity per artwork, material and adhesive, finish, shape, application format, artwork readiness, freight and the number of labels that remain usable in production.
- Small production teams comparing hand labeling with bottle applicators should confirm roll direction, core size, label gap, roll diameter, container consistency and placement tolerance before buying equipment.
- Tapered bottle label fit depends first on container geometry: moving to a straighter panel, reducing label height, using a shaped dieline or separate front/back labels can reduce wrinkles and edge lift.
- Frozen vacuum bag labels should be selected around application temperature, frost or condensation, bag flexibility, storage handling and barcode placement on the final packed package.
- Multi-SKU short-run label planning should control artwork versions, quantities, dielines, barcodes, roll packing and obsolete inventory risk by SKU.
- Stock packaging with custom labels usually favors test launches and flexible SKUs, while fully printed packaging is more suitable when demand, artwork and package specifications are stable.

- Small food brands often need guidance on label size, ingredients and allergen layout space, nutrition panel space, barcode placement, waterproof material selection and small batch proofing.
- Beverage and wine buyers often need guidance on BOPP, PET, wet-strength paper, cold bottles, condensation, cooler or ice bucket use, curved glass surfaces, roll direction and adhesive review.
- Food label layout planning should reserve room for product identity, net quantity, ingredient list, allergen declaration, nutrition panel when required, barcode or QR code, date or lot code area and storage directions.
- Clear BOPP labels support transparent no-label looks; white BOPP labels support stronger color, small-text readability and barcode contrast.
- Wine label material choices should account for dry shelf use, cellar storage, refrigeration, ice bucket handling, premium paper appearance and regulatory label review.
- Small brands often compare DIY product label printing with factory-made custom labels when they are deciding between flexibility, waterproof performance, color consistency, roll format and small-batch MOQ.
- Buyers comparing custom label MOQ often need a practical answer for whether 100 pcs is enough for market testing, samples, product photography, early retail trials and design validation.
- Roll label buyers often need plain-language guidance on roll direction, outside or inside winding, core size, label gap, dispenser use and labeling machine compatibility.
- Small beverage brands often compare can labels vs printed cans when deciding between lower-risk flavor testing, plain can inventory, seasonal artwork, cold drink handling and high-volume printed can programs.
- Label size decisions should account for the usable label panel, package curve, seams, taper, copy volume, barcode area and whether the buyer needs front labels, back labels or wraparound labels.
- Matte vs gloss label decisions should separate appearance from performance: finish affects glare, color feel and photography, while material and adhesive determine wet, cold or oily package suitability.
- Front/back labels and wraparound labels answer different buyer tasks: separate panels support clean branding and detailed copy, while wraparound labels support fuller coverage when the container shape and application method allow it.
- Barcode and QR code label planning should account for contrast, quiet space, curved surfaces, clear film, small label size, proof scanning and whether the code belongs on a front label, back label or wraparound label.
- Removable vs permanent adhesive decisions should match the buyer task: temporary campaigns and reusable packaging may need clean removal, while retail product labels usually need stronger long-term adhesion.
- Custom die-cut label planning should consider shape complexity, rounded corners, bleed, safe area, fragile points, roll setup and whether the shape fits the real package surface.
- Label artwork file setup should confirm vector PDF or AI files, bleed, trim line, safe area, CMYK color mode, outlined fonts, image quality, barcode clarity and dieline setup before proof approval.
- Pantone vs CMYK label printing decisions should separate screen color from print color and account for material, finish, white ink strategy, brand color targets and proof review.
- Co-packer and production-line label orders should confirm roll direction, core size, label gap, maximum roll diameter, SKU counts, extra setup labels, carton marks and shipping destination.
- Label lamination decisions should connect finish choice with real handling risks, including moisture, oil, scuffing, refrigeration, shipping friction and premium shelf presentation.
- Paper vs film label decisions should start from the food package environment: dry boxes and jars may fit paper, while chilled, oily, wet, clear or flexible packaging often needs BOPP or PET film.
- Tamper seal label planning should match shape, bridge length, adhesive and roll setup to the actual jar lid, box flap, cup edge or takeaway package opening.
- Sauce and condiment label decisions should account for oily residue, refrigeration, curved bottles, edge lift risk, film material choice, adhesive selection and protective finish.
- Coffee label planning should separate coffee bags, cafe cups and cold brew bottles because each package has different surface, storage, moisture and layout needs.
- Date code and lot number label planning should reserve a readable marking area, avoid tight curves and confirm whether the code changes by batch before fixed artwork is approved.
- Bottle label troubleshooting topics include peeling, edge lift, smudging, condensation, oily residue, cold application, curved bottles, oversized wraparound labels and material or adhesive mismatch.
- Buyers should confirm final regulatory wording with the responsible brand, producer, importer or compliance professional for the destination market.
